title: Descriptive Statistics II: Skewness, Kurtosis, Measures of Dispersion
summary: Skewness (positive/negative); percentile-based kurtosis; range; inter-quartile range; standard deviation; coefficient of variation; mean deviation.
objectives: Define skewness and identify positive/negative skew.
Calculate range, IQR, standard deviation and coefficient of variation.
revision: Skewness = asymmetry. Positive: mean > median, tail right. Dispersion: range, IQR, SD, CV, mean deviation. SD = √(Σ(X−M)²/N).
traps: Positive skew: mean > median (tail pulls mean toward tail).
SD is more stable than range or mean deviation.
confusions: Confusing direction of skew with position of mean.
Using range instead of IQR for skewed data.

notes.t: The asymmetry of a distribution. A distribution is skewed when it is not symmetrical.

r: Difference between highest and lowest scores
Average distance of scores from the mean
SD expressed as percentage of mean
Average of absolute deviations from mean

notes.t:
Worked example: Scores 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Mean M = 6.
Deviations: −4, −2, 0, +2, +4. Squared: 16, 4, 0, 4, 16. Sum = 40.
Variance = 40 / 5 = 8. SD = √8 ≈ 2.83.
Positive skew: mean > median; negative skew: mean < median. SD is the most stable measure of dispersion. Frequently tested in UGC NET.

OCR-extracted from source page 142: In a positively skewed distribution, Mean > Median > Mode. In a negatively skewed distribution, Mean < Median < Mode. In a symmetrical distribution, Mean = Median = Mode.

mnemonics.title: PAN
mnemonics.text: Positive skew: tail right, mean > median. Negative skew: tail left, mean < median.
